findings.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἂν τυφλῷ ἐντελλόμενος ἐδείκνυεν
findings.english_quote: for he would not have given directions to a blind man while commanding him
findings.issue: “Given directions” obscures the distinction between showing or pointing something out, expressed by ἐδείκνυεν, and issuing the command, expressed by ἐντελλόμενος. Although an instructional sense of δείκνυμι is possible, the argument about physical blindness particularly supports retaining the showing/pointing language. The note lists that alternative but the main wording reduces both verbs to instruction.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “for he would not have pointed it out to a blind man while commanding him.” Retain a note explaining that “pointed it out” represents showing or indicating the tree without specifying a particular physical gesture. Submit the revised wording to fresh review.

findings.source_quote: εἰ κατὰ τὴν κραυγὴν αὐτῶν τὴν ἐρχομένην πρὸς· μὲ συντελοῦνται
findings.english_quote: whether they are acting in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me
findings.issue: The action-oriented interpretation is possible, but unqualified “are acting” suppresses the completion or carrying-through component of συντελοῦνται. The draft's note acknowledges this component and supplies a completion-based alternative; leaving it only in the note does not give the main wording the same lexical transparency. This concerns translation wording, not corruption of the verified print.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “whether they are carrying matters through in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me,” retaining the note on the chosen interpretation and its completion-based alternative. Review the replacement afresh without changing the supplied Greek punctuation.
